description: Hi everyone! I’m a CSE student interested in space technology, software development, and simulation. I want to build a Space Debris Removal Mission Simulator focused on orbital trajectories, debris capture, and mission optimization. I can contribute programming, research, and problem-solving. I’m looking for teammates skilled in Python, AI/ML, physics, orbital mechanics, 3D visualization, or UI/UX. Let’s collaborate and build something innovative!
summary: Project Ysoriel is a browser-based Space Mission Design Game that turns the abstract trade-offs of mission design into something players can experience. In the Mission Design Studio, players choose a destination (Earth orbit, the Moon or Mars), then select a launch vehicle, spacecraft bus, propulsion, solar array, antenna and science instruments. Live checks on budget, launch mass, power, delta-v and data downlink must all pass before launch. The mission is then simulated through launch, orbit insertion, commissioning and six months of science operations, with outcomes rolled against reliability and design margins, and ends in a graded debrief. A second module, Orbital Guardian, lets players run a debris-removal tug in a crowded orbit, managing fuel, risk and timing. Together they let students experience a complete mission from concept to operations, see how every choice shapes success, and build intuition for space sustainability. It runs in any browser with no installation.
details:
What it does. Project Ysoriel has two connected modules. The Mission Design Studio asks players to design a mission under real constraints: budget, launch mass, power, delta-v, science return and data downlink. Choices interact. More instruments add science but also mass, power draw and data. Farther destinations cut launch capacity, weaken the data link and delay commands. The flight simulation then rolls launch, orbit insertion, commissioning and six months of operations against vehicle reliability and the player's margins. The result is a score with feedback on what limited the outcome. Orbital Guardian is an operations game about removing orbital debris with a tug.

Benefits and impact. Students rarely get to experiment with a whole mission from concept to operation. Ysoriel makes those trade-offs tangible and shows why margins, reserves and balanced design matter more than building the biggest spacecraft. It also builds awareness of orbital debris and space sustainability.

How it works. The model uses the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation for delta-v, solar flux that falls with distance from the Sun (Mars receives about 43% of Earth's), downlink capacity that falls with distance, one-way light time, and simplified reliability and anomaly models. Values are educational and simplified.

Tools. HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript (Canvas animation), with a Node.js server and a JSON scores API. The 7-slide demo was built with pptxgenjs.

Creativity and factors considered. We combined engineering design and operations in one platform, gave every part meaningful trade-offs, and made failure educational. Accessibility, mobile layout and zero-install play were design priorities.
